decision_q1: Option (a) full state-transition-first: write s.settledAt before the external transfer loop. Do NOT adopt option (b) two-pass, and do NOT add a separate executing reentrancy flag.
rationale_q1: HIGH-1 is the CEI inversion at executeSettlement:262-274 — the external token.transfer loop (263-271) runs BEFORE s.settledAt is written (274). The reentrancy guard is the settledAt != 0 check at line 257, which is still 0 throughout the loop, so a hook-bearing token (or a seat contract that calls back) can re-enter executeSettlement mid-loop and re-run the payout loop. Option (a) closes this with a single SSTORE move: writing s.settledAt before the loop makes any re-entrant call hit the line-257 guard and revert with AlreadySettled. No additional flag is needed because settledAt is the unique terminal marker for execute (the refunded flag is a separate leg, blocked by fullyConfirmedAt != 0 at line 288). Option (b) two-pass (validate+snapshot then interact) is rejected: it buys nothing over (a) for this single-guard case, adds a storage snapshot (gas + complexity), and does not fix the loop-internal gap any better than (a) — the guard must be set before the first external call either way. Per-seat pull-claim reentrancy gaps ruled out: (1) claimedMask updates — executeSettlement does NOT mutate confirmedMask or expectedMask; those are frozen at initiate/confirm, so there is no mask-write to reorder inside the loop. (2) escrowBalance decrement ordering — executeSettlement does NOT touch escrowBalance (initiateSettlement already debited it at line 212; see prior audit H2), so there is no escrowBalance write to reorder inside the loop. The only state write inside or after the loop is settledAt, and moving it before the loop eliminates the entire reentrancy surface. The per-seat transfer loop itself is safe under CEI because each token.transfer is a single external call with no further state mutation between calls; once settledAt is set pre-loop, a re-entrant executeSettlement cannot pass line 257. This matches the discipline refundSettlement already follows (refunded=true at 289 before the transfer at 291).
test_plan_q1: 1) Forge golden (reentrancy): deploy a malicious hook-token whose transfer() calls back into executeSettlement(settlementId) on the first seat; assert the inner call reverts with AlreadySettled and the outer completes paying every seat exactly once. 2) Forge golden (happy path): N-seat bill, full confirm, window elapsed, execute; assert each seat received payouts[idx] exactly once, escrowBalance unchanged by execute, settledAt set, re-execute reverts AlreadySettled. 3) Invariant fuzz (foundry): invariant { token.balanceOf(address(this)) >= escrowBalance } AND { escrowBalance >= sum of unclaimed settlement totals } must hold at every internal point — i.e., the shadow var never exceeds the actual token balance and never drops below the sum of settlements still owed. Run with a hook-token target to exercise the reentrancy path under fuzzing. 4) Re-run the existing 41/41 FastTandaBillV2 twin suite (run 266) against the reordered execute to confirm no golden drift. 5) Static: Slither/forge-lint reentrancy flag on executeSettlement should clear once settledAt precedes the loop.
decision_q2: Option (a) SafeERC20-style internal wrapper, vendored (OpenZeppelin SafeERC20 or equivalent), applied to BOTH the executeSettlement transfer loop and the fundEscrow transferFrom. Do NOT adopt (b) allowlist as the primary guard, and do NOT adopt (c) delivered-amount reconciliation as the primary guard.
rationale_q2: HIGH-2 is that the all-or-nothing revert assumption (comment 265-266) only holds if the token reverts on failure. A token that returns false (no revert) or partially sends lets the loop pay seats 0..k, set settledAt, and strand the rest with no refund escape (refund blocked by fullyConfirmedAt != 0). Option (a) is the correct primary guard because it converts the silent-failure class into a hard revert: SafeERC20's low-level call + success/return-data check reverts on (i) call failure, (ii) no return data, and (iii) return data that is not bool true. This makes the existing all-or-nothing semantics actually true for any ERC-20, including USDC/CCTP on World Chain 480, without restricting the token set. It is the minimal, standard, audited fix and matches what refundSettlement's require(token.transfer(...)) already assumes but does not enforce. Option (b) allowlist + admin-gated extension is rejected as primary because it (i) conflicts with invariant 1 (no key custody / no recovery / logic-only) by introducing an admin-gated mutable allowlist, (ii) is brittle — a new CCTP-minted or bridged USDC variant on World Chain 480 would require an admin action, and (iii) does not protect against a token that is allowlisted but later changes behavior. Option (c) delivered-amount reconciliation (accept delivered vs claimed) is rejected as primary because it changes the lossless split invariant: accepting a partial delivery means the sum of payouts no longer equals unsettled, breaking the deterministic escrowBalance==0 proof (prior audit H2) and requiring a new reconciliation state machine. It is a viable fallback only if a token is known to under-deliver by design (fee-on-transfer), which USDC/CCTP on World Chain 480 are not. Recommendation: vendor SafeERC20 (do not hand-roll — the return-data edge cases are exactly where hand-rolled versions fail), apply to both external-call sites, and keep the require(...) style so the typed TokenTransferFailed error is preserved. What option (a) does NOT protect against: (1) fee-on-transfer / rebasing tokens that deliver less than requested but still return true — SafeERC20 sees a successful transfer and does not reconcile the delivered amount, so the split math silently under-pays; this is out of scope for USDC/CCTP on World Chain 480 (both are non-fee, non-rebasing) but must be documented as a hard precondition. (2) A token that returns true but does not actually move funds (hostile/buggy token) — SafeERC20 cannot detect this without a balance-delta check, which option (c) would add. (3) Over-funding stranding of the owner's own excess (prior audit F-5/LOW) — unrelated to the transfer path. (4) The 256-transfer gas ceiling (MED-3) — SafeERC20 does not reduce gas; a max-size settlement may still be unexecutable by a single tx.
test_plan_q2: 1) Forge golden (no-return token): deploy a token whose transfer() returns no data; assert safeTransfer reverts (SafeERC20 StandardTokenTransferFailed) and the settlement does NOT set settledAt — no partial stranding. 2) Forge golden (false-return token): deploy a token whose transfer() returns false; assert safeTransfer reverts and the loop aborts atomically with no partial payout. 3) Forge golden (USDC/CCTP World Chain 480 twin): use the existing FastTandaBillV2 twin with a standard USDC mock; assert full payout, escrowBalance==0 after execute, no drift. 4) Invariant fuzz: invariant { token.balanceOf(address(this)) >= escrowBalance } under a hook-token + false-return-token + no-return-token target set; the SafeERC20 wrapper must keep the all-or-nothing property under all three. 5) Re-run the 41/41 run-266 suite against the SafeERC20-wrapped execute to confirm no golden drift on the standard-token path. 6) Static: confirm no remaining bare token.transfer / token.transferFrom calls outside the SafeERC20 wrapper (grep).

ADR-0010 (Permit2 single-tap funding) is not present as a local file under docs/adr/ on this lane; it is referenced in bridge docs (SR-002, OPP_HARLEY_002, XIXI_WORLDCHAIN_ADDENDUM F5). The Permit2 deposit path is a separate Wave-2.5 UX item and does not interact with the HIGH-1/HIGH-2 fixes except that fundEscrow's transferFrom is also wrapped by SafeERC20 in this verdict — a future Permit2 depositWithPermit must use safeTransferFrom-equivalent semantics or its own success check to avoid reintroducing the silent-failure class.

Option (a) for Q2 does NOT protect against fee-on-transfer / rebasing tokens that return true but deliver less than requested (SafeERC20 sees success and does not reconcile delivered amount). USDC and CCTP-minted USDC on World Chain 480 are non-fee, non-rebasing, so this is out of scope, but it must be documented as a hard precondition in NatSpec. If a fee-on-transfer token is ever supported, option (c) delivered-amount reconciliation becomes necessary on top of SafeERC20.

The 256-transfer gas ceiling (prior audit MED-3) is NOT addressed by either fix. A max-size (256-seat) fully-confirmed settlement may still be unexecutable by a single tx under paymaster per-tx caps, with no refund escape (fullyConfirmedAt != 0 blocks refund). This remains a v3 item (batched execute with a paidMask, or a documented payout-loop seat cap). It is flagged here so the PC execution card does not assume the hardening resolves the gas ceiling.

The fundEscrow CEI inversion (prior audit MED/F-7: transferFrom before escrowBalance +=) is a separate finding from HIGH-1. This verdict's Q2 diff wraps the transferFrom in safeTransferFrom but does NOT reorder it relative to the escrowBalance credit. Under a hook-bearing token, a re-entrant fundEscrow could still double-increment escrowBalance without matching token balance. Recommend the PC execution card also apply the debit-after ordering (credit escrowBalance after the safeTransferFrom) or drop the shadow var, per prior audit F-7. This is out of scope for the two HIGHs but is the root of the escrowBalance/balance drift class.

Both fixes are additive and preserve the existing typed errors (TokenTransferFailed, AlreadySettled) and the lossless split invariant (sum(payouts) == unsettled). No ABI-breaking changes: no new external functions, no signature changes, no storage-layout changes (SafeERC20 is a library, no storage). Clone compatibility is preserved.
gas_notes: Q1 (CEI reorder): moving the s.settledAt SSTORE from after the loop to before it is gas-neutral in total — it is the same single cold-then-warm SSTORE, just relocated. There is no additional SSTORE; the slot (settlements[i].settledAt) is already touched by the struct push at initiate. Net gas delta: ~0 (the write happens at a slightly different point in the call sequence but the same number of SSTOREs). No new warm-slot cost. Q2 (SafeERC20 wrapper): each safeTransfer/safeTransferFrom adds a low-level call + returndata-size check + a decode of the bool. For a standard token that returns true, this is ~2-5k gas per call over a bare transfer (the extra CALL for the return-data check and the SLOAD-free decode). For a 256-seat execute, that is ~256 * ~3k = ~768k additional gas over the bare loop — non-trivial but small relative to the ~9M baseline of 256 USDC transfers. For the single fundEscrow call, the delta is ~2-5k. The wrapper is a net gas increase, not a decrease, but it is the cost of converting a silent-failure stranding class into a hard revert. If gas becomes a constraint on the execute path, the SafeERC20 wrapper on the execute loop can be made conditional (wrap only if the token is not the known-good USDC address) — but that reintroduces the allowlist complexity and is not recommended for MVP.
